1. The animation shows that paying extra on a mortgage earns a guaranteed return equal to the loan's interest rate. It uses a character named Tessa, labeled "illustrative", and a rate of 7.40% from an Oct 8, 2026 survey. That rate becomes a "bar" that any other use of the money would have to clear.

2. Over the six frames, a dollar bill starts beside Tessa's house. Then a gray bar appears with the bill on it. The bar is labeled "the bar: 7.40% a year, before taxes" and is measured against a zero line. Next, the text "interest no longer charged" appears under the bar. Last, a dashed, faded bill labeled "any other use" appears off to the side. In the final frame that label gains the words "not tested".

3. Putting a dollar toward the mortgage saves 7.40% a year in interest, before taxes. Investing the same dollar would have to beat 7.40% to come out ahead. The animation does not say whether any alternative would do that, and the "not tested" label shows it did not test one. The footer on every frame says "US only · history, not a forecast".

4. The animation gives no explicit advice. A viewer might take away that 7.40% is the number to compare other options against. That is a framing of the question, not a recommendation to pay down the loan or to invest.

5. None of this was stated outright. The comparison to a 7.40% bar came from the animation, but any "pay extra" or "invest" conclusion would be my own. The on-screen text ("not tested", "history, not a forecast") deliberately avoids recommending either one.
